scope: First practice passage only, source 00:37.33–01:23.70; not the full 34-minute video
timing: Approximate transcript alignment; only noted tilt/extrusion intervals were measured from source frames
evidence_limit: Current official documentation is not an archived verification of every statement at publication time

scenes.transcript: So I come from the Genie One world.
scenes.intended_understanding: Identify the product the guest is discussing.
scenes.composition: Begin with the static guest placeholder full-frame, then move into the white-grid composition with the same placeholder on the right and a large Genie One card on the left.
scenes.assets: Static fictional presenter; official Genie mark if available under suitable terms; product name. No invented product UI.
scenes.reason: Presenter establishes context; the single card creates a stable referent for the next sentence.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Open on a full-screen product UI. That is useful for an original explainer, but starts at a detail level the reference has not introduced.
scenes.motion_plan: Trigger the graphic transition on the product introduction. Exact transition frame still needs source measurement; do not assume the current render is ground truth.
scenes.clarity_check: One product, one name, one speaker. Do not depict the product family yet.

scenes.transcript: Genie One is our AI co-worker for business users.
scenes.intended_understanding: Know the intended audience and basic role.
scenes.composition: Keep the same card and right speaker tile. Add the short subtitle “For business users.” Give product name more weight than the subtitle.
scenes.assets: Existing product card; two text levels. No new metaphor or AI-generated artwork.
scenes.reason: This sentence defines an audience. A stable labelled card supports that distinction without implying a mechanism.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: A business-person icon beside a chat window makes the role more concrete; reserve that for an approved adaptation because the reference uses the product card.
scenes.motion_plan: Reveal the audience with “business users”; hold the card long enough to read.
scenes.clarity_check: Avoid adding dashboards, integrations and ontology all at once.

scenes.transcript: It connects to your data and tools.
scenes.intended_understanding: Understand that the product can use data and connected tools.
scenes.composition: Shrink the known product card toward the center-left; show a database cylinder on its left and a tool symbol on its right. Keep the presenter fixed. Labels: “Data” and “Tools.”
scenes.assets: Consistent Fluent database/tool symbols; existing product card; straight connectors.
scenes.reason: Keeping the product preserves continuity while the two new endpoints explain the added relationship.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Show real connector settings. More concrete, but too much UI detail for this approximately 2.4-second sentence.
scenes.motion_plan: Shrink first, reveal endpoints, then connectors. Source arrows are a visual connection metaphor; label them and do not imply a specific API request sequence.
scenes.clarity_check: No moving particle stream or claimed bidirectional synchronization. This sentence says connection, not execution order.

scenes.transcript: It answers questions about your business.
scenes.intended_understanding: See what a business question and a useful answer look like.
scenes.composition: Replace the small connection diagram with the large rounded chat panel on the left; keep the speaker right. Show the reference question “Which products generated the most sales?” then the three result cards.
scenes.assets: Reconstructed illustrative chat. Reference totals: Laptops $40,800; Monitors $20,540; Accessories $10,200. These are source illustration values, not live evidence or a product benchmark.
scenes.reason: A question and answer demonstrate the capability more clearly than abstract boxes labelled “Question” and “Answer.”
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: An official UI capture is more authentic for a product tutorial, but a different capture would change this reconstruction and require an appropriate matching example.
scenes.motion_plan: Typed question → submitted question bubble → answer label and result cards. At about 2.4 seconds, full typing and detailed results may be too fast; prioritize source timing, and propose longer narration only if adaptation is approved.
scenes.clarity_check: Readability risk: the viewer cannot inspect all values in this short beat. The next beat retains the results.

scenes.transcript: It acts on the answers that it gives you
scenes.intended_understanding: Recognize an action that builds on the returned insight.
scenes.visual_type: Action added to the same chat
scenes.composition: Retain the question and result cards. Reveal the reference suggestion “Create campaign for top-selling products” below the results.
scenes.assets: Same illustrative chat; one action row. No generated marketing photograph is needed.
scenes.reason: Retaining the answer makes the consequence clear: the action uses the result instead of starting an unrelated task.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Show a completed campaign or tool execution. Reject for this scene: it would claim a result the reference illustration does not establish.
scenes.motion_plan: Reveal the action with “acts.” Hold the final question/results/action state through the governance sentence.
scenes.clarity_check: This is an illustrative suggested action, not proof that a campaign was created. Actual execution depends on supported tools and configuration.

scenes.transcript: all within the governance framework that you already have.
scenes.intended_understanding: Understand that existing access controls still apply.
scenes.composition: Scale down the same chat panel; draw the reference green outline and shield marker around it. Keep the presenter stable.
scenes.assets: Same chat; Fluent shield-lock symbol; boundary. Production note can identify governance without adding a large unsupported headline to the source layout.
scenes.reason: The boundary adds one constraint to a mechanism the viewer already understands. It preserves visual continuity.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Show two users with different permissions and allowed/denied records. This explains governance better in a standalone tutorial, but needs a separate beat and should not be squeezed into this reconstruction.
scenes.motion_plan: Keep the chat visible while resizing. Introduce the boundary on the governance phrase, then hold.
scenes.clarity_check: A shield is shorthand. Do not imply unrestricted access becomes safe merely because a border appears. Current docs describe permission-aware access.

scenes.transcript: But Genie One sits in a larger stack of AI co-workers and other AI tools on Databricks. So, for example,
scenes.intended_understanding: Place the known product within a broader product family.
scenes.composition: Return to the same product card, change its plane and extrude peach layers behind it. Keep the top card recognizable and the presenter fixed.
scenes.assets: Existing product card plus repeated card backplates; no new images.
scenes.reason: The known object changes into a family metaphor. This matches the reference and prepares the comparison.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Flat product-family header with three equal cards. It is less likely to imply a technical stack, but departs from the reference and reveals products ahead of the narration.
scenes.motion_plan: Measured source card tilt: about 55.167–55.700; layer expansion: about 55.833–56.300. Hold after settling; do not keep rotating.
scenes.clarity_check: Stacked cards are an editorial metaphor, not evidence that these products execute in a layered dependency chain.

scenes.transcript: if Genie One is our agent for business users,
scenes.intended_understanding: Recall the first role before contrasting it with another.
scenes.composition: Keep Genie One central and in front of the stack. Add the curved “For Business Users” annotation above it.
scenes.assets: Existing card, one label and one curved leader.
scenes.reason: The annotation makes the comparison criterion explicit before the next product is introduced.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Use a two-column audience table. Good for a summary, but premature before the second role is named.
scenes.motion_plan: Add the label on “business users.” Keep the card position stable.
scenes.clarity_check: Use a leader line for annotation, not an arrow suggesting data flow.

scenes.transcript: Genie Code is our agent for technical users. It helps them write code and do other work within the lakehouse.
scenes.intended_understanding: Distinguish a technical-work product by audience and activity.
scenes.composition: Reveal Genie Code left of Genie One, at the same visual plane. Preserve the central stack. Add the reference lower-left note about writing code and working within the lakehouse.
scenes.assets: Named Code card; consistent product mark treatment; readable activity note.
scenes.reason: Sibling position communicates product-family membership; the words explain the meaningful distinction.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Show a notebook or code-editing demo. Better for demonstrating the workflow, but a new demo would interrupt the family comparison; propose it for a later dedicated beat.
scenes.motion_plan: Reveal the product when named. Add the activity annotation when writing code is mentioned. Keep text clear of overlapping cards.
scenes.clarity_check: Do not use a gear as an unexplained technical-user symbol. Code is broader than autocomplete, but do not add unrelated current capabilities to the historical narration.

scenes.transcript: We also have Genie Agents, which can be accessed by both types of users.
scenes.intended_understanding: Introduce the domain specialist and distinguish access from role.
scenes.composition: Reveal Genie Agents to the right of Genie One. Keep all three product names readable. Add the source subtitle indicating business and technical audiences.
scenes.assets: Named Agents card and short audience subtitle; no anthropomorphic robot illustration.
scenes.reason: This completes the family without resetting the scene. Shared access is stated separately from specialization.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Draw two audience lanes converging on Agents. It makes access clearer, but introduces another diagram in the middle of the reference family layout.
scenes.motion_plan: Reveal Agents on its name, then the audience subtitle on “both types of users.”
scenes.clarity_check: Do not add arrows implying Genie Code calls Genie Agents unless the script and evidence establish that mechanism.

scenes.transcript: And they're really focused on domain-specific work. They're essentially domain experts.
scenes.intended_understanding: Understand specialization as curated business context.
scenes.composition: Retain the three-card family. Add the reference curved annotation under Genie Agents: “Focused on domain-specific work.”
scenes.assets: Existing family plus one role annotation. Optional Sales/Finance example belongs in an approved adaptation, not silently in the reconstruction.
scenes.reason: The additional label explains the third product’s distinction while the first two remain visible for comparison.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Zoom into a Sales agent with curated tables, definitions and example questions. More concrete and educational, but needs extra screen time and a separately approved scene.
scenes.motion_plan: Add the role annotation with “domain-specific work,” then hold the completed family.
scenes.clarity_check: Domain expert is a metaphor, not a promise of correctness. Do not represent Agents as omniscient AI.

scenes.transcript: And I can actually cover that in more depth if we want to.
scenes.intended_understanding: Recognize a conversational handoff rather than a new concept.
scenes.visual_type: Return to presenter; no new graphic
scenes.composition: Cut to the full-frame static fictional guest placeholder, matching the source scene change.
scenes.assets: Reuse the approved static presenter; no new imagery.
scenes.reason: The speaker is offering elaboration. A new diagram would introduce information the narration does not teach.
scenes.alternative_and_tradeoff: Hold the family diagram. It is economical but misses the reference’s conversational cut.
scenes.motion_plan: Source speaker cut around 81.53 seconds. Keep captions within their reserved band.
scenes.clarity_check: A static placeholder is intentional. Do not add synthetic lip motion or imply it is the original speaker.

authorization: User explicitly requested generating all storyboard graphics for comparison in the latest message.
